Get started

Source: SITE_START.md

Stable GitHub release · version 0.4.3. Not yet published on CRAN. Advanced methods retain documented scientific limitations.

Install the stable GitHub v0.4.3 release

Requires R 4.2 or newer. Install from a known branch or commit rather than silently using an unspecified development state:

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github(
  "stefanosbalaskas/eyetrajectories",
  ref = "v0.4.3",
  dependencies = TRUE
)
library(eyetrajectories)
packageVersion("eyetrajectories")

The exact qualified source archive is available from the stable GitHub release; verify SHA-256 38f7b8eb05c71c3a0c4c266cc590b9afdb73906b0d9412cf52185523f649da5e.

Start with the native R API

Native R methods do not require Python to initialize. The exported functions and examples are documented in the function reference; a useful starting point is the trajectory construction, validation and functional decomposition family.

library(eyetrajectories)

# Inspect the native trajectory constructor and its input contract.
help("etr_trajectory_set", package = "eyetrajectories")

# Explore the documented native principal component analysis.
help("etr_fit_mfpca", package = "eyetrajectories")

Read the help topic before selecting coordinate-system assumptions, units, missing-data policies and estimation settings. These commands access documentation; they do not execute analyses or imply independent scientific certification.

Optional published Python 1.2 backend

For explicitly Python-backed operations, install the matching Python version and configure reticulate to use it. Read Python bridge for the procedure and for the distinction between wrapper availability and native R parity.

Choose a scientific workflow before running an estimator

Open the Research Workflow Portal to inspect the structure of a local CSV in your own browser, declare a scientific target and compare ten verified native R workflow mappings. It is a navigation tool, not an estimator, and no CSV is uploaded.

Navigate the site

  • Research workflow portal: local CSV preflight, method-selection wizard, ten real R workflow references and boundaries.
  • Methods: which methods and assumptions belong to which analysis family.
  • Reference: auto-generated R help pages.
  • Validation: evidence categories, tests and limits on scientific claims.
  • GitHub repository: exact code, issues and current development activity.
